narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Rhythm on Wood: The Story of Clog Dance
This is clog dance. 19th century to present.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (BT9naCq0fdE)
Title card: clog dance · United Kingdom · 19th century to present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Clog dance encompasses traditional step dance forms defined by percussive footwear across Wales, Northern England, the Netherlands, and North America.
Over time, European clog traditions contributed to the development of tap dance and American clogging.
on_screen: Map: United Kingdom · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Practised historically in community settings, educational physical culture, and stage entertainments, combining athletic training with joyful rhythmic expression.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers execute percussive footwork on hard surfaces.
The steps demand physical accuracy, strength, balance, and large body movements, often combined with theatrical pantomime appropriate to the character of the piece.
Watch for Clog step strike.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (BT9naCq0fdE)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Stationary or linear progression on hard floors
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Accompaniment relies on strict rhythm, historically featuring string ensembles (fiddle, viola, cello, piano) or banjos.
Classical arrangements like Percy Grainger's 'Handel in the Strand' prescribe tempos between 120 and 132 BPM.
Listen for the Fiddle, Viola, Cello, Piano.
The pulse is 2/4 or 4/4 at about 126 beats a minute.
Bright, steady instrumental chamber or string music driven by strict temporal rigidity to support loud percussive wooden shoe striking.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned
Listen later: Clog Dance: Handel in the Strand — Percy Aldridge Grainger; Wooden Shoe Clog Dance — Charles C. Bertholdt
Waveform or rhythm-pattern graphic: Rigid in time, fast percussive pulse
scenes.music: the music brief's underscore at its own tempo; drop narration under the hook of a verified recording if licensed, else original

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The defining attire consists of clogs with rigid wooden soles.
Dancing requires a hard floor surface capable of echoing the percussive strikes of the footwear.
on_screen: Image gallery: 6 licensed images with attribution
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Composer Percy Aldridge Grainger designated his work 'Handel in the Strand' for clog dancing; Charles C. Bertholdt published 'Wooden Shoe Clog Dance' for banjos in 1890.
Variants include Welsh stepdance, Northern English clog dance, Dutch Klompendansen, clog Morris, and American clogging.
Direct ancestor to modern tap dance and related percussive step traditions.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: clog dance is child of tap dance: Tap dance developed in part out of clog dancing.
clog dance is variant of Welsh stepdance: A style of clog dancing unique to Wales.
clog dance is variant of clogging: An American style derived from earlier clog traditions.

Instruments: Fiddle, Viola, Cello, Piano, Banjo. Vocal style: Instrumental performance. Form: Sectional dance arrangement. Mood: Fast, Merry, Rigid, Vigorous.
